summary: Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She held a faculty post at the University of Warsaw around 1989.

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a B.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by David Germano, and an M.T.S. from Harvard Divinity School.

Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. His career includes serving as Assistant Director at Boston University and holding an attested appointment at Marymount Manhattan College in 2008.

Brandon Dotson is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich, where he worked from circa 2010 to 2016.
Brandon J. Harwood completed his Ph.D. at the University of Louisville, where he was advised by Patrick Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) was an Indologist and historian. He earned a master's at the University of Calcutta and a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1980–1985). He served as an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University from around 1992 to 2020.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, he served as a research fellow at Kyoto and Otani Universities, and became an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology between circa 1963 and 1967 and was a student of Geshe Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1999–2018) before becoming Kazushige Hirasawa Professor of Japanese Studies at Bates College in 2018.

Brian Daizen Victoria works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. After studying at Komazawa and Temple universities, his career included posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, and a senior lectureship at the University of Adelaide (2005–2015).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Buddhist studies. He received his Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara and served as a Mongolian language lecturer at UC Berkeley and Numata Center.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology educated at East India Company College and Fort William College. He served as the British Resident in Nepal from 1833 to 1843.

Brian J. Nichols is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his Ph.D. from Rice University under the supervision of Anne C. Klein.

Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned her Ph.D. from the UCL Institute of Archaeology. She was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge, and served as Secretary General of the European Association of South Asian Studies.

Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna, where she earned her doctorate (Promotion) and later served as an extraordinary university professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin).

Bronwyn Finnigan works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Auckland under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop, she held appointments at Auckland and Marquette University before becoming an Associate Professor at the Australian National University in 2014.

Brook Ziporyn works in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan under Donald J. Munro and has served as the Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago.
Brooke Schedneck specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.
